core_obligations: Apply the localness definition to the situation, using that etale localness on the source-and-target implies localness on the source (proof lines 7811-7814).

Forward direction: choose etale neighbourhoods of x' and y', transfer the property to the composite f composed with g', descend to f' over the neighbourhood by clause (4), then to the ambient f' by clause (3), and conclude x' lies in W(f') (proof lines 7816-7827).

Reverse direction: from x' in W(f') obtain a neighbourhood on which f' has the property, descend to U' to V' and then to U' to Y, take the image U of U' in X, which is open because etale morphisms are open, and use clause (1) for the etale covering to conclude that U to Y has the property and hence x lies in W(f) (proof lines 7829-7843).
proof_roadmap: Applicability of the localness definition (proof lines 7811-7814).
Forward direction through clauses (1), (4) and (3) (proof lines 7816-7827).
Reverse direction with the etale covering and openness (proof lines 7829-7843).
difficulty_reason: For a property P of morphisms of schemes which is etale local on the source-and-target, and a commutative diagram of schemes with points such that the two vertical maps are etale at the relevant points, the lemma shows that a point x lies in the locus W(f) exactly when x' lies in W(f') (statement lines 7786-7808). The proof is a two-direction argument using the defining clauses of etale localness on the source-and-target: the forward direction picks etale neighbourhoods, transfers the property to the composite using clause (1), descends it to f' over the neighbourhood using clause (4) and then to the ambient f' using clause (3); the reverse direction runs the same clauses in the opposite order and additionally uses that an etale morphism is open, so that the image of the etale neighbourhood in X is an etale cover of it, and clause (1) then transfers the property back to X (proof lines 7811-7844). The claim is H2: the content is a careful but finite application of the clauses defining the localness notion, with both directions written out in full.
